problem.text: The tensor diagnostic's existing exclusion predicate did not cover paths containing global_vars[, local_vars[ or updated_globals[. The patch adds those three spellings.

reasoning.text: Filtering inside collect suppresses matching tensor references before result recording, without changing traversal or freeing tensors.

impact.text: The whole-parent-tree literal search found an import in quantize.py but no invocation of list_gpu_tensors. The demonstrated scope is diagnostic reporting, not a newly activated conversion path.

source_notes.text: The earlier debugger-filter entry describes adding dbg.value_resolve_thread_list; this patch retains that exclusion.
Issue #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate”, reports a native-extension import failure, not debugger-reference filtering.

limitations: No live debugger session, tensor traversal or CUDA behavior was tested; the computation tested only a transcribed string predicate.
Literal searches do not exclude dynamic or external callers. The provenance of the three new path spellings in debugger internals remains unverified.

claims.text: list_gpu_tensors traverses globals, thread frames, attributes, dictionaries and sequences. collect applies tensor/device and size checks, then path exclusions, before grouping references by tensor identity for size-sorted, per-device tables. The patch changes only the exclusion list.

The added strings match indexed paths produced by dictionary and sequence traversal. Matching is substring-based, not debugger-object detection: ordinary application paths containing those strings are also suppressed, while another unfiltered reference can still expose the same tensor.

A standard-library predicate transcription newly excluded examples for all three added strings, retained model.weight and model.global_vars_weight, and preserved the existing debugger-thread exclusion. It also excluded model.global_vars['weight'], illustrating the name-based boundary.
This favors a small diagnostic-output filter over debugger-aware traversal pruning; it does not establish reduced traversal cost or memory use.

annotation.summary: Extends tensor-diagnostic path filtering with three debugger-style indexed-variable names, leaving traversal and tensor lifetime unchanged.

argv:
import json
old=['.stderr.dbg.','dbg.value_resolve_thread_list']
new=old+['global_vars[','local_vars[','updated_globals[']
paths=['worker.global_vars[\'weight\']','local_vars[0]','updated_globals[\'x\']','model.weight','model.global_vars_weight','model.global_vars[\'weight\']','worker.dbg.value_resolve_thread_list[0]']
print(json.dumps([{ 'path':p,'old_skip':any(x in p for x in old),'new_skip':any(x in p for x in new)} for p in paths]))
